name: cloud-vault
description: Diego's Cloud Vault — standalone Vaultwarden client Android app. Hosts vault.diegonmarcos.com (self-hosted Vaultwarden) in a dedicated BrowserHostFragment APK with the constellation updater. Extracted from Cloud SuperApp's vault section (libs:vault was a KeePassDX stub) in favour of the full Vaultwarden web-app experience. Build via Nix devShell, one APK out.

vault._doc: Bitwarden-fork rebuild of this app — THE shipping Cloud-Vault.apk since 2026-08-18: CI's push-triggered job runs materialize-fork + build-fork and publishes the fork APK as Cloud-Vault.apk (GHCR :latest + GH release rolling tag). build.sh's default `build`/`release` still produce the legacy WebView wrapper, now a manual-only CI fallback. Uses the SAME fork machinery ac_cloud-mail's forks.mail entry uses (see cloud-mail-engine.sh, ported verbatim into this app's build.sh).

build._doc: Module `app` (applicationId com.x8bit.bitwarden upstream, com.diegonmarcos.cloudvault after patch 0001) is the password manager — NOT `authenticator`, a different product in the same repo. Flavor `fdroid` (dimension `mode`) is the Google-free flavor: Firebase/Crashlytics/ML-Kit/Play-Billing are standardImplementation-only and GoogleServices/Crashlytics tasks are disabled for fdroid in afterEvaluate. No release signingConfig is declared upstream (app/build.gradle.kts release buildType has none) so the APK comes out unsigned from gradle; build-fork's unconditional _enforce_signature re-signs it with the ONE shared constellation key regardless — no 'signing' key needed here.
build._build_blocker_doc: com.bitwarden:sdk-android is resolved from https://maven.pkg.github.com/bitwarden/sdk (settings.gradle.kts dependencyResolutionManagement), which 401s without an authenticated GitHub account/token even for public artifacts — verified un-buildable anonymously (local sandbox). settings.gradle.kts reads the credential as: password = userProperties["gitHubToken"] (rootDir/user.properties, gitignored, local-dev only) ?: System.getenv("GITHUB_TOKEN") ; username is hardcoded to "" (empty). RESOLVED in CI (run 31602029574, 2026-08-12): the auto-minted per-run GITHUB_TOKEN reads bitwarden/sdk packages fine — no BITWARDEN_PACKAGES_TOKEN PAT needed (the workflow still prefers that secret if ever set). Locally, put a token in user.properties. Not a gradle_props entry — it's a plain env var upstream settings.gradle.kts reads.

vault.comment: Bitwarden Android (password manager). Rebrand + self-hosted-server-default + NOTICE patches in ac_cloud-vault/patches/. materialize-fork is pure git clone+patch (no network auth); build-fork VERIFIED green in CI 2026-08-12 (run 31602029574, signed 36 MB fdroid/release APK) and promoted 2026-08-18 to the push-triggered publisher of Cloud-Vault.apk.

signing._doc: ONE shared Cloud-constellation signing key for ALL Android apps (Cloud-Comms hub+forks, Cloud-Nav, Cloud-Wallet, Cloud-Browser, Cloud-Vault, Cloud-IDE, Cloud-SuperApp). The SAME key signs every app so cross-app signature-IPC + the in-app fleet updater never hit a signature mismatch. KEY LOCATION (raw credential + sops passwords live ONLY in the vault repo): Shared/Providers/D_TOOLS-DEVICES/d2-android/release.jks (OU=Cloud Constellation) + Shared/Providers/D_TOOLS-DEVICES/d2-android/signing.secrets.yaml. build.sh::_resolve_signing resolves $VAULT_DIR (default ~/git/cloud-vault) + sops-decrypts the passwords, exporting ANDROID_KEYSTORE_FILE/ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD/ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS/ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD which the gradle signingConfig reads. CI does the same via a vault checkout + the SOPS_AGE_KEY secret. THERE IS NO FALLBACK: if the key is unavailable the build FAILS LOUD.

diagnostics._doc: On-device DevControlServer diagnostics → cloud sink. Baked into BuildConfig.LOG_SINK_URL / LOG_SINK_STREAM by app/build.gradle. Empty url = cloud push disabled.

modules._doc: Shared modules the SHIPPING fork (the vendored Bitwarden tree at this app's root, :app:assembleFdroidRelease) includes BY REFERENCE; settings.gradle.kts names them as literals, it does not iterate this map. Declared so the ship workflow watches them and the publish gate hashes them. The previous map (app.depends_on core/browser/updater, analytics) described the legacy WebView wrapper's Groovy settings.gradle, which looped over it; that wrapper was deleted in 2b5afeca0 and Bitwarden's settings never read the map, so none of those modules was ever compiled into Cloud-Vault.apk.

ui._doc: #868 THE nav declaration (libs:bottomnav NavDecl): ui.bottom_nav is the island, ui.sections[] what each item opens, ui.default_section where the app opens. The ids are Bitwarden's four unlocked tabs (VaultUnlockedNavBarTab); the Send tab drops out at run time when the org disables Sends. Each tab's own sub-screens are Bitwarden's navigation graph, not page strips, so no section has pages.

auto_update._doc_max_installs_per_pass: Most install sessions ONE unattended background pass may open. A background pass cannot show the system install dialog (Android 10+ blocks background activity starts), so each install it starts leaves a tap-to-install notification holding a PackageInstaller session until the user answers it. Unbounded, one pass over the 40-entry fleet opens 40 and the installer hits Android's 50-session cap - 'Too many active sessions for UID'. The remainder is picked up by the next pass. User-initiated 'Update all' is NOT capped: it runs in the foreground where the dialog appears and sessions resolve at once.

analytics._doc: Consumed by :libs:analytics, which reads THIS file (rootDir) at build time and bakes the values into BuildConfig. Both backends are single-site today, so every app reports into the same site and is told apart by .app — give each app its own site_id once per-app sites exist in Umami/Matomo.

web._doc: #876 Cloud Vault as a Kotlin/Wasm page (web/ is its own gradle root; the shared libs' pure-Compose sources arrive through the ab_cloud-libs-shared/web composite). Rendered into 1_cicd/src/cicd/ship-cloud-vault-wasm.yml by the workflow generator: `./gradlew wasmJsBrowserDistribution` in `dir`, tested by test/test-vault-web.sh, `build/dist/wasmJs/productionExecutable` zipped to `artifact` and attached to the rolling release as `gh_asset`. A mocked page: the island and tab strips are ui.bottom_nav / ui.sections as the Android shell reads them, the first section shows mock data and the rest say they live in the Android app. The APK's own ship ignores this directory.

unit._doc: The Bitwarden fork's JVM suites (src/test, no emulator). The fork job of the ship workflow runs this task's autofill + matching suites plus AuthRepositoryTest (a failed refresh never wipes the vault, the persisted re-auth flag, the token-only re-auth) and the fleet package (OfflineStatusTest) before anything is published; the whole app suite is ~470 classes and not that job's question.

configs_pages._doc: Configs > General and Configs > About (libs:ui-nav-bars fleetconfigs, rule 1_cicd/src/data/configs-pages.json, #1352 v2). general.sections: the anchors of the one General page, in order (perms, battery, storage, notifications, ui, language are required; app opens this app's own Configs; update is added after perms by default). about: the hand-written part of the extensive About: tagline, description, features, screens, guide, privacy, backends (ids of ac_cloud-account/build.json::fleet_endpoints, resolved to mesh URLs at build time), related fleet apps, credits for a fork. Permissions, data stores, crash/analytics libs, name, icon, version, build sha and date, repo, licence, origin, crash sink, debug API and changelog are derived, never typed here.

about.tagline: Passwords and secure notes on your own server
about.description: Cloud Vault is the fleet's password vault over the owner's self-hosted Vaultwarden: logins and secure notes, Send for sharing a secret once, a password generator and autofill into other apps. It is a signed fork of the Bitwarden client. It exists so passwords are held on infrastructure the owner controls, never on a commercial password service.
features: Vault of logins and secure notes
guide: Sign in to the owner's Vaultwarden server.
Use Generator when creating an account.
about.privacy: No ads and no third-party trackers. A crash report is saved on the phone and sent only to the phone's own C3 WebServer over loopback; nothing leaves the device unless you share it. It talks only to the fleet services listed below, over the private mesh first.
about.credits: Upstream: the Bitwarden Android client (github.com/bitwarden/android), GPL-3.0, by Bitwarden Inc. The server is Vaultwarden (AGPL-3.0). The fleet build adds its update, crash and configs libraries.

perms._doc: #1360 every grant this app needs, by libs:perms catalogue id (needs), and the fleet apps that do work for it with the grants THEY must hold (helpers). The ONE declaration: generated into assets/app-perms.json (cloud-android-perms-guard.py --write), drawn by Configs > General > Perms (libs:perms AppPermsSection) with live state, Grant / Open and Grant all, asked at first run (first_run), and reported as 'Missing permission X - Grant' when an operation fails (PermsGate). perms-guard fails when code uses a gated API or another app's engine that is not declared here, or when the manifest and this list disagree.
